claim: The CAS refsnaplog migration covers `cas_ref_log` objects at `_log/<txn_id>` and `cas_ref_snap` objects at `_snap/<snapshot_id>`, moving both from binary codecs to the phase-1 text file shape.
`cas_ref_log` and `cas_ref_snap` are materialized whole with a decompressed line-reading loop; they have no streaming reader, `seek`, `getStream`, or offset index.
A `cas_ref_log` object represents exactly one committed `RefLogTxn`, containing one namespace, one transaction ID, and that transaction's vector of `RefOp` entries.
A normal reference transaction is limited by `ref_txn_max_ops = 1000`; a transaction containing `RemoveNamespace` is a removal-class transaction subject to the 64 MiB byte budget.

Refsnaplog objects are written through `putIfAbsentControlled` or `backend.putIfAbsent`, not `putDeterministicArtifact`, so their deterministic encoding is a correctness property rather than a byte-adoption gate.
The recovery seal is an ordinary `RefTableSnapshot` published at synthetic `snapshot_id = {my_epoch-1, UINT64_MAX}` with `sealed_from` set to the greatest applied reference transaction ID.
`sealed_from` is an optional `RefTxnId` whose absence and presence must remain distinguishable in the snapshot wire format; it is not represented by a sentinel value.
Every `RefTxnId` field in refsnaplog text, including the synthetic seal sequence `UINT64_MAX`, is serialized as a decimal string rather than a JSON number.

A live snapshot has no `remove_txn_id`; a removed snapshot has `remove_txn_id` and empty `committed` and `precommits`; and every snapshot satisfies `snapshot_id >= *sealed_from` when `sealed_from` is present.
`cas_ref_log` keys use the `Always` `.zst` suffix, while `cas_ref_snap` keys replace their `.proto` suffix with `.zst`.

`decodeRefLogTxn(data, expected_ns, expected_txn_id)` and `decodeRefTableSnapshot(data, expected_ns, expected_snapshot_id)` reject a body whose namespace or transaction/snapshot ID differs from the key-derived expected values.
Refsnaplog codecs retain validation of canonical clean `ref_name` values and non-zero `ManifestRef` and `RefTxnId` fields.
Snapshot committed rows are strictly ascending by `ref_name`, precommits are strictly ascending by `(ref_name, manifest_ref)`, and every precommit has `kind == Precommit`.
Both refsnaplog formats belong to the `Control` family with `Tolerant` keys, `Always`/`.zst` storage, `object_cap = 64 MiB`, and `line_cap = 64 KiB`.
Refsnaplog text headers stamp `v = G_BUILD = 3`; this migration does not bump `G_BUILD` or append a `changePoints` entry.
The refsnaplog conversion is a pre-release hard cutover with no legacy-binary-to-text dual-read fallback.
`RefOwnerBinding` and `RefOwnerKind` are shared by the ref log and snapshot codecs in `Core/Formats/CasRefWireVocab.{h,cpp}` so peer codecs do not depend on one another.

Owner-transition bindings use flat `o` and `n` key prefixes rather than nested JSON objects because the flat `JsonObjectReader` has no array or nesting support and extending it would increase the blast radius.
The `cas_ref_log` text shape is a `cas_ref_log` header, a meta line containing `ns`, `we`, and `rs`, one record line per `RefOp`, and a `{"n":count}` trailer.
The `cas_ref_snap` text shape is a `cas_ref_snap` header, a meta line containing lifecycle and optional removal/seal fields, committed and precommit record lines, and a `{"n":count}` trailer.
Refsnaplog text uses `we`/`rs` for the primary `RefTxnId`, `rte`/`rts` for `remove_txn_id`, `sfe`/`sfs` for `sealed_from`, and `me`/`mb`/`mo` for `ManifestRef` fields.
`cas_blob_meta` is a three-scalar `Control` object containing `state`, `condemn_round`, and `size`, converted from the fixed 22-byte `CAMT` binary codec to one-line JSON text.
`cas_blob_meta` uses `Never` compression, so its stored bytes are the text itself and `blobMetaKey` remains unchanged without a `.zst` suffix.
Blob-meta JSON encodes `state` as `clean` or `condemned` and encodes `condemn_round` and `size` as decimal strings.
`MetaState::Clean` means the blob is referenceable and present, while `MetaState::Condemned` means GC found zero in-degree but the body remains present and may be resurrected by a writer CAS.
Blob-meta lifecycle operations use the backend etag `Token` for conditional updates; they do not use a byte comparison of the encoded meta body.
The condemned-state gate remains correct when the text codec round-trips `state`, `condemn_round`, and `size`, because dedup and GC branch on decoded fields and CAS-swap by etag.
`BlobMeta.version` remains in the in-memory struct with default value `1` for `CasInspect`, but is not serialized because the header `v` is the authoritative format version.

`loadMeta`, `putMetaIfAbsent`, `casMeta`, and `deleteMetaExact` remain in `Core/CasBlobMeta` while `MetaState`, `BlobMeta`, `encodeBlobMeta`, and `decodeBlobMeta` move to `Core/Formats/CasBlobMetaFormat`.
Malformed, truncated, wrong-type, unknown-state, and over-cap blob-meta input maps to `CORRUPTED_DATA`, while a future `v` or unknown `!` key maps to `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.
The blob-meta cutover deletes the `CAMT` binary codec in one pre-release commit and performs no binary-to-text dual read.
Blob-meta text stamps `v = G_BUILD = 3` without adding a new format generation or `changePoints` entry.
`cas_blob_meta` was never a protobuf object; it used the `CAMT` fixed binary format, so its migration has no protobuf-graveyard work.
The `cas_run` object is the GC source-edge in-degree data plane and is converted from `CARN` block-framed binary to sorted NDJSON with a typed header, one record per line, and a {"n":count} trailer.
`Core/CasRunFile.{h,cpp}` remains after the `cas_run` cutover because `CasManifestCodec` still embeds a `RunKind::ManifestEntries` `CARN` stream; phase 6 owns its eventual deletion.
`cas_run` remains a streaming object: it has `object_cap = 0`, is read sequentially one NDJSON line at a time, and keeps only O(one line) resident.

Random access is removed from `cas_run`: `RunFileReader::seek`, `inDegreeInGeneration`, and `SourceEdgeKeyCodec::seekPrefix` are dead, and full sequential reads are required by the whole-file checksum model.
Every `cas_run` consumer must stream the whole object, accumulate its checksum, and verify it against the referencing `RunRef.checksum` before the records affect a deletion decision.
The `cas_run` checksum uses the same streaming chained CityHash128 routine on write and read, covering the entire stored object including header, records, and trailer.
The streaming checksum changes the checksum value from the former one-shot `cityHash128(run_bytes)` algorithm because `object_cap = 0` forbids materializing a run for hashing.
`cas_run` is `RecordStream` with `Strict` keys and `PinnedRaw` storage, and its byte-deterministic output is required for `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption.
The record-stream codec is backend-free and operates on caller-owned `ReadBuffer` and `WriteBuffer`; backend stream ownership stays in `Core/CasBlobInDegree`.

Malformed, truncated, trailer-count-mismatched, checksum-mismatched, unknown-kind, out-of-order, duplicate, and over-`line_cap` run data is rejected with `CORRUPTED_DATA`; future `v` and unknown `!` keys use `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.
Only `RunKind::SourceEdge` is live for standalone `cas_run`; `BlobDelta` and `TargetShardDelta` are dead, while `ManifestEntries` remains only for the embedded part-manifest stream.
A source-edge record maps to JSON keys `b` for the algo-prefixed lowercase blob reference, `s` for a 32-character lowercase-hex source ID, and `m` for `edge`, `zero`, or `condemned`.

String sorting by `(b, s)` must equal the existing binary `(algo, digest, source_id)` byte order; fixed-width lowercase hexadecimal rendering makes this property hold by construction and it is pinned by a golden test.
The production fold uses a hand-written two-cursor merge of the prior run stream and scattered deltas; no k-way line-based merger is introduced.
The `CasBlobInDegree.h` documentation claiming that `previewDeletes` uses `inDegreeInGeneration` is false; `previewDeletes` uses `zeroInDegree` and a raw `kCondemned` scan.

The part-manifest-cleanup run has no reader: actual cleanup executes inline from the in-memory `folded.mf_cleanup` map, so the durable cleanup run and fold-seal `part_manifest_cleanup` field can be removed without changing the delete driver.
If the approximately 2x NDJSON byte cost proves to be a bottleneck in soak, the only planned fallback is to re-binarize `cas_run` behind the same typed-open API; no fallback is pre-built.
`cas_part_manifest` becomes a `PayloadHybrid` object consisting of a header line, descriptor meta line, sorted JSON entry records, a {"n":count} trailer, and a raw payload zone for inline bytes.

The part manifest remains one object; its embedded `CARN` `RunKind::ManifestEntries` stream is replaced inside the same body by JSON entry lines and a trailer, with no separate object and no `CasRecordStreamFormat` reuse.

Each inline manifest entry is represented by an `il` length in its JSON record, while its arbitrary bytes are stored after the trailer as a banner line, exactly `il` raw bytes, and a newline; EOF must follow the last segment.
Blob manifest entries carry `ha`, `h`, and `sz`; inline entries carry `il` and no blob reference; entry records are sorted by canonical path without duplicates.
Part manifests are read whole after `openObject`; there is no on-disk random access, `getStream`, or `seek` requirement for their entry records.
Part-manifest integrity is provided by the whole-object zstd frame, `payload_digest`, the entry-count trailer, and fsck rather than the deleted per-block `CRC32C` framing.

Part manifests are `Tolerant` and `Always` compressed but are not `Strict`, `PinnedRaw`, or a `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption gate; identity-keyed persistence uses `putIfAbsentControlled` and exchange re-hashes content.

`CasRecordStreamFormat` and the fixed-offset blob-envelope codec are not reused for part manifests because the former is source-edge-specific and the latter supports only one raw payload rather than multiple banner segments.
Manifest keys migrate from `.proto` to the `Always` `.zst` suffix, `parseManifestKey` strips `.zst`, and persistence actually applies `sealObject` and `openObject`.

`encodePartManifest` returns canonical uncompressed text for text-size budgeting; backend PUTs seal that text, backend GETs open it before decoding, and exchange remains text-to-text without wrapping.

Part-manifest encode and decode enforce canonical paths, ascending order with duplicate rejection, valid blob references, mutually exclusive Blob/Inline placement fields, namespace/ref matching, and entry/encoded-byte caps.
`payload_digest` is CityHash128 over the canonical text body with the digest rendered as zero hex during hashing, and decoding recomputes and verifies it.
Part-manifest text stamps `v = G_BUILD = 3`, drops the binary `writer_version`, uses `Tolerant` JSON keys and `Always`/`.zst`, and has no dual-read path.
Phase 6 deletes `Core/CasRunFile.{h,cpp}` after the part-manifest cutover because the embedded manifest stream is its last remaining `CARN` user.
The blob envelope is a fixed-length 256-byte JSON header: a JSON object, ASCII-space padding, and a newline at byte 255, with the payload beginning at the header length.
The envelope decoder parses JSON from byte zero and then requires every remaining pre-newline header byte to be an ASCII space; any other byte or missing newline is `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The envelope's ref budget is `(L - 1) - PREFIX.size() - SUFFIX.size()`, with `L` equal to the pool's `blob_header_len`; the ref is incrementally escaped and truncated without splitting an escape.
The envelope uses a codec-local ref escaper that leaves `/` unchanged, escapes quotes, backslashes, and control characters, and makes byte-budget arithmetic independent of global JSON settings.
Envelope JSON maps `tag`, `bld`, and `by` to 32-character lowercase hex strings, `ts` and `ch` to JSON numbers, `op` to a full word, and `ref` to the locally escaped diagnostic string.
The envelope drops `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version`; `CityHash64` is no longer part of envelope processing.
The blob envelope keeps `blobKey` unchanged, uses `Never` compression, and leaves the payload as raw bytes at the derived fixed offset.
The envelope header is built before payload streaming, so header construction has no payload dependency and remains compatible with S3-native staging.
Bad envelope type, truncation, pad violations, duplicate keys, and over-256-byte headers are `CORRUPTED_DATA`; future `v` and unknown `!` keys are `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.
`ObjectKind`, `ProvenanceOp`, `Provenance`, and the slim `EnvelopeHeader` move with the envelope codec into `Core/Formats/CasBlobEnvelopeFormat`, while `CasEnvelope.{h,cpp}` are deleted.

The fetch-handoff retention-pin design was superseded on 2026-07-23 by a publish-confirm design in which the receiver confirms the sender's committed ref before promoting; the superseding design removes the pool-global pin and GC changes.

The original fetch-by-relink correctness hole was that the sender released its part before the receiver committed its ref, leaving no in-degree overlap during a sufficiently long precommit stall; the affected reports were `#42` and `#43`.

Transport-level seals such as sender ACKs, response suffixes, HTTP trailers, and full-duplex reverse channels were rejected because Poco interserver transport is half-duplex and response-side data cannot provide a reverse acknowledgement or backpressure.
The shared retention-overlay primitive folds current refs together with the edge sets of live-owner pins, and a blob is condemnable only when its source-edge set is empty across that union.

Retention pins may encode their protected edges as either an explicit manifest closure or a snapshot window; the primitive is agnostic to payload shape and distinguishes consumers by ownership and liveness.
The superseded v1 protocol proposed a build-owned pin at `gc/fetch-pins/<receiver_srid>/<build_id>` containing the fetched part's blob-ref closure, created by the sender before releasing its part.
In the superseded handoff protocol, the sender returned the manifest address and pin ID in the existing response, and the receiver deleted the pin only after its own ref commit.
The superseded protocol's zero-gap ordering was `[sender-ref] → [sender-ref + pin] → [pin] → [pin + receiver-ref] → [receiver-ref]`, so the sender created protection before releasing its part.
Under the superseded protocol, a failed sender pin PUT aborted relink and used byte-stream fetch, while a sender or receiver failure left the pin to be reaped rather than risking data loss.
The proposed fetch-pin reaper used the existing `min_active` build-watermark floor from `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`, not a wall-clock TTL.
The proposed reaper deleted `gc/fetch-pins/<srid>/<build_id>` when `build_id < srid.min_active` or when the owning `srid` was terminated, fenced, or lease-expired.
The superseded design required verifying that the receiver's `min_active_fn_` covers an in-flight fetch/relink build for the entire fetch; this was its single stated integration point.
Bulk write-replica warm-up was recorded as a future extension of build-owned pins, using a union of many manifest closures or a snapshot-window payload.

The detached/relink cluster recorded `B66b` as extending same-pool relink into `to_detached` and `B66a` as a separate local-backend atomicity issue for shared detached refs; both were orthogonal to the pin mechanism.
Until the pin or publish-confirm mechanism lands, the fetch-by-relink tail was explicitly accepted and documented; a bespoke relink handshake was not to be built in the interim.

The source-layout refactoring is an approved design whose goal is a readable self-describing CAS tree with strict one-direction includes, selected file merges, and decomposition of `CasStore` and `CasBuild`, with zero behavior change.
The source-layout refactoring includes the final renames `Cas::Store` → `Cas::Pool` and `Cas::Build` → `Cas::PartWriteTxn`, after layout and decomposition phases.

The refactoring fixes both dependency-direction violations rather than documenting around them; the backend-to-`CasTextFormat` violation disappears when v3 codecs own `sealObject` and `openObject`, so no `SealingBackend` decorator is planned.
The refactoring cannot start until all eight CAS codecs-v3 migration steps are landed and green.
After codecs v3, `Formats/` contains per-object format files and includes only IO primitives and identifier vocabulary, never `CasBackend.h` or subsystem headers.
The target tree removes `Core/` and organizes CAS code into `Primitives`, `Formats`, `Backend`, `Pool`, `Gc`, `Tools`, `Parts`, and top-level facades.
The canonical include direction is `Primitives → Formats → Backend → Pool → Gc → Tools ≈ Parts → facade`; `Tools` and `Parts` are siblings with no edges between them.

The include-direction rule is documented in `README.md` and is not enforced by a CI script; deliberate exceptions allow the staging sweeper and `probeConditionalCopy` to bypass `Backend` into `IObjectStorage`.

The remaining post-v3 direction violation is `CasEvent.h` including the envelope header for `toEventKind`; the mapper is to move into `Formats/CasBlobEnvelopeFormat.h` so `CasEvent` can become dependency-free.
The refactoring merges files rather than classes, keeps type names and APIs unchanged during the merge phase, and places types/enums before codecs before logic in merged files.
Per-object `Formats/` files are deliberately not merged because their one-object-per-file organization is a settled codecs-v3 decision.
Decomposition follows state and lock ownership boundaries: every component owns its mutexes wholesale, no lock changes the state it covers, and no lock-acquisition order changes.

`Pool/CasRefLedger` owns ref-table state and locks, ref transaction allocation and queueing, recovery/seals, snapshot publication, stale-precommit sweeping, cache eviction, remount/shutdown coordination, and ref read/lifecycle entry points.
`Pool/CasMountRuntime` owns mount fencing, lease keeping, self-remount state, writer epochs, build-sequence watermarks, active builds, `minActive`, and build-sequence allocation/retirement.
`Pool/CasManifestReader` owns manifest reads, token-gated byte-weighted decode caching, and location lookup, while `CasPlainObjects` owns namespace-file and mountpoint-object operations.
The decomposed `CasPool` remains a composition root with thin delegating wrappers so external wiring, GC, tools, and tests retain their existing API.
`Pool/CasBlobUploader` moves byte-delivery execution out of `CasBuild`, while admit/adopt/resurrect decisions and dependency-set recording remain on the transaction class.
The renames change only C++ identifiers and file names; persisted bytes, key layouts, log/error/event text, ProfileEvents, metric names, and protocol vocabulary remain unchanged.
`PoolConfig` is split into `RefLedgerConfig` and `MountConfig` slices while the aggregate `PoolConfig` remains public and external callers remain unchanged.

The migration phases are merges, moves, `CasStore` decomposition, `CasBuild` decomposition, renames, and a final CA-default stateless run plus short ca-soak; each phase is gated by a build and full CAS gtest battery.

The source-layout invariants prohibit persisted-byte, key-layout, log/error/event, metric, lock-coverage, and lock-order changes, and require move commits to contain no content edits and content commits to contain no moves.
The revised one-pipeline design supersedes the staged-intent, subclass, and two-phase disk-transaction variants for `[TXN-ONE-PIPELINE]`.

Every CA disk transaction mutation updates one transaction-private overlay at call time, and the existing disk `commit` is the only operation that publishes the overlay into the durable CAS namespace.
An open CA transaction has a single mutable view: reads combine the overlay with committed state and observe preceding writes, renames, and deletes from the same transaction.

The transaction states are `Open`, `Committed`, and `Aborted`; in `Open`, writes, creates, hardlinks, deletes, moves, directory moves, and ref moves update the overlay immediately without publishing live refs.

`commit` freezes the overlay, constructs manifests, runs the internal CAS build protocol, promotes blobs, publishes or moves refs, applies final overlay state, and is the only durable publication point.
Blob bytes and metadata may be eagerly staged on a private local or S3 backend while a transaction is open, but they are not reachable through a live ref until commit.
Deletes are applied to the overlay immediately rather than stored in a second replay list; therefore create → delete → create leaves the path present in the final overlay.

A CA-specific disk `precommit` phase is rejected because the relevant `Keeper`/disk ordering is general to real disk transactions, while a CA-only phase would add an extra visibility boundary and upstream conflict surface without solving the general problem.

The existing replicated flow remains `MergeTreeData::Transaction::renameParts` → `Keeper::tryMultiNoThrow` → `MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit` → `IDataPartStorage::commitTransaction`; the one-pipeline design does not change those call sites.

If a process terminates after a successful `Keeper` multi but before disk commit, existing recovery finds the missing part, fetches it from another replica when possible, or invokes `onPartIsLostForever` and `createEmptyPartInsteadOfLost` while accounting `lost_part_count`.

`DiskObjectStorageTransaction::dispatch` applies an operation immediately when `transactionIsStagingOverlay()` is true and otherwise queues it for FIFO replay; CA uses the eager path and ordinary object storage keeps the deferred path.

`DiskObjectStorageTransaction::commit` and `tryCommit` validate in release builds that an eager transaction has an empty `operations_to_execute` queue, preventing methods that bypass `dispatch` from silently creating a second timeline.

`writeFileImpl` uses the generic `tryCreateWriteBuffer` transaction hook; CA supplies its hash-on-write staging buffer while the default implementation returns `nullptr` for unchanged metadata behavior.
An autocommit write buffer retains its owning disk transaction and invokes the existing `commit` from its finalize callback; it does not invoke a new `precommit` phase.

The CA overlay covers part-file entries, pending blob payloads, removals, projection and part-directory re-keying, committed-ref changes, and table-level or mountpoint mutations reached through the transaction.
For a staged tmp-to-final part move, `ContentAddressedTransaction::moveDirectory` only re-keys the transaction view and does not call `publishStaging`; durable ref operations occur at commit.

The one-pipeline design removes B151 early publication and `rename_published_refs`, while B183 temporary text-index state must remain represented in the overlay so a scratch ref cannot overwrite the authoritative final manifest.
Before commit, `undo` or transaction destruction discards the overlay, abandons builds, and removes private staging without mutating the shared live namespace.

There is no atomic backend operation spanning several refs, so existing commit-time compensation for refs newly created before a later publication failure remains necessary; dropping an existing ref is not valid rollback for a failed repoint.

The design rejects deferred delete intents, disk-queue replay before commit, replay in a new `precommit`, reuse of `IDataPartStorage::precommitTransaction`, `publishStagedData`, publication from `moveDirectory`, and a CA-specific transaction subclass or split base.
